signals.title: NOK/EUR — G10 Bilateral Theme + Crude Shock
signals.text: NOK leads the weekly G10 board gaining an average of +1.639% across its peer basket, while EUR anchors the laggard slot at −0.649% across 9 pairs. This creates an extreme 2.288% bilateral spread that clears the critical threshold. WTI crude rallies +2.62% to $104.70/bbl on Middle East supply disruption risk following geopolitical tensions involving Iran, providing an immediate terms-of-trade impulse for NOK. The divergence is reinforced by monetary fundamentals, with Norges Bank at 4.5% versus the ECB at 2.65%, generating a +185bp nominal spread favoring the Krone alongside a +1.42% real policy rate advantage. EUR/USD downtrend structure remains fully entrenched below its SMA20 (1.1206) and SMA50 (1.1402) clusters, compounding the broad-based weakness in European currencies. Trade bias: Long NOK/EUR; energy shock and policy divergence favor further widening. Catalyst: Norges Bank policy decision on 5 Nov. Risk: Immediate geopolitical de-escalation drives crude back below $100/bbl, eroding NOK's terms-of-trade outperformance.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Downside Skew + Fed Divergence
signals.text: USD/JPY spot trades at 157.45, compressed below its SMA20 (157.91) and SMA200 (158.52) in a tight 20-session box. The Saxo 1M 25-delta Risk Reversal prints at an extreme −2.24 put skew, signalling heavy institutional bidding for downside protection despite a wide rate differential. At the same time, OIS carry basis shows SOFR at 3.94% versus TONA at 1.23%, maintaining a +271bp carry advantage that structurally rewards the dollar. CFTC positioning shows JPY Leveraged Funds net short −25,598 contracts (pctl 94, z +1.43), indicating the short base has substantially rebuilt over the trailing year. The options market is aggressively pricing tail-risk hedging against potential intervention or carry compression near 160.00 while spot remains range-bound. Trade bias: Neutral/range USD/JPY; heavy options put skew constrains upside despite positive carry. Catalyst: US Election cycle and upcoming FOMC rate path decisions. Risk: A clean technical breakout above 158.52 forces downside put decay and re-engages the carry grind toward 160.00.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded Speculative Short + Retail Divergence
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1156, remaining structurally heavy below its SMA20 (1.1206), SMA50 (1.1402), and SMA200 (1.1566) moving averages. Leveraged Funds positioning sits deeply crowded at net short −94,138 contracts (week ending Oct 20), placing it in the 2nd percentile of its 52-week range with a z-score of −1.72. Conversely, retail sentiment on Retail sentiment data registers an extreme 86% long positioning, setting up an active institutional-versus-retail divergence. The macro backdrop continues to penalize the euro, as Fed policy at 4.0% against ECB at 2.65% enforces a 135bp carry advantage favoring the dollar, compounded by German October headline CPI softening to 2.8% YoY. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; macro carry and spec positioning dominance override contrarian retail positioning. Catalyst: next ECB meeting (mkt: 61% hike priced) on 17 Dec. Risk: Retail capitulation coinciding with short covering pushes spot back above the SMA20 at 1.1206.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Rates Momentum + Technical Reversal Setup
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3387, positioning between its rising SMA20 (1.3294) and SMA50 (1.3386) as short-term price action turns against the broader intermediate downtrend. UK 2Y sovereign yields stand at 4.91% against US 2Y at 4.67%, with the 2Y yield spread shifting +26bp over 5 sessions and +30bp over 20 sessions in sterling's favor. UK Economic Surprise Index holds positive at +10.2, reflecting persistent domestic data resilience ahead of monetary policy events. However, policy rates show Fed at 4.0% versus BoE at 3.75%, leaving a narrow 25bp carry premium favoring USD that caps aggressive trend extension. Trade bias: Bullish GBP/USD; short-term yield momentum and technical structure favor further consolidation higher. Catalyst: Bank of England policy decision on 5 Nov. Risk: A daily close below the SMA20 at 1.3294 negates the short-term technical reversal structure.
